name:        useClickableContainer
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Makes a container element clickable while preserving nested interactive element behavior. Solves the "nested interactive elements" problem: when a card is clickable but contains buttons/links, clicking those should NOT trigger the card's action. Detects interactive ancestors between the click target and the container, and ignores text selections. Supports href navigation (including middle-click and Ctrl/Cmd+click for new tabs).
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useClickableContainer

name:        useInteractiveRole
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Resolves what a polymorphic component should render as, in one place: href wins, then onClick, then an interactive trigger context supplied by a parent (Popover, DropdownMenu and friends), then inert. Use it in any component that is sometimes a link, sometimes a button, and sometimes plain content; Token, Thumbnail, Item and ClickableCard all do. Because context is part of the resolution, a component built on it becomes a valid trigger for new surfaces without changing.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInteractiveRole

name:        useClipboard
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Copy-to-clipboard behavior: the clipboard write, a transient isCopied flag with its own reset timer, and an optional polite screen-reader announcement. Extracted so every copy affordance is a thin control over one implementation instead of re-deriving the timer and announcement. Rapid re-copies restart the reset timer so the confirmation always lasts the full duration, and the timer is cleaned up on unmount. CodeBlock and Timestamp build their built-in copy buttons on it; reach for it directly when building a copy affordance that is not a plain icon button (a menu item, a labeled text button, a copy-on-click value chip).
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useClipboard

name:        createReorderable
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core
description: Makes a collection's rows reorderable. On a touch screen a finger held still on a row's handle for a moment picks it up (a flick on the handle still scrolls): the row stays in its place, dimmed, while a copy of it follows the finger and an accent line marks where it would land; the other rows stay still, the page scrolls near its edges, and on release the rows rearrange. A pen held still on a handle where the primary pointer is coarse picks the row up as a finger does. A mouse, or a pen where the primary pointer is fine, drags a handle at once the same way, and the rows take their places without motion; a cancelled drag puts everything back at once. Without a drag, the handle toggles reorder mode for its row (a click, Space or Enter): each arrow key moves the row a place at once, and Escape or another activation ends the mode, keeping the moves; screen readers hear each move with the row's place and neighbours, and a hint shows the moves and Done as buttons, for taps alone. The reorder code ships with this function: a collection without the prop loads none of it.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook createReorderable

name:        useCalendarConstraints
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Calendar
description: Provides date constraint validation for calendar views and custom range pickers. It combines boundary dates, span limits measured from an in-progress range start, and custom rules (such as weekly closures or blackout dates) into an isDateDisabled predicate. Calendar uses it internally to disable day buttons; use it directly when building bespoke scheduling interfaces or range pickers.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useCalendarConstraints

name:        useCombobox
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Selector
description: Tracks the active option of a single-select combobox and handles its keys, while DOM focus stays on the control. It powers Selector and CommandPalette; use it to build a combobox those components do not cover, including one over a single-line text field you render yourself, such as a search field whose results replace a page section, or an "add people" field in a dialog. It renders nothing: you render the field, the listbox and the options, and spread `getFieldProps`, `getListboxProps` and `getOptionProps` onto them, or wire `role`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant` yourself from `onKeyDown` and `getItemId` for a control such as a button.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useCombobox

name:        useInputContainer
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Makes an input container wrapper clickable, delegating focus to the inner input/textarea when the user clicks non-interactive areas (icons, padding, status indicators). Built on top of useClickableContainer, so nested interactive elements (clear buttons, calendar toggles, links) are handled safely; clicking them does NOT steal focus from the input. Automatically detects input type: text-like inputs receive .focus(), while other types (checkbox, radio, file) receive .click().
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInputContainer

name:        useInputStatusIcon
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Builds the on-field status affordance for a bordered input and its accessibility wiring, so every input in the family behaves the same for a given status. The attached variant renders a plain glyph and leaves the text to the message box; the detached variant renders nothing here, because the message box already carries its own icon; the tooltip variant renders a real focusable button whose tooltip is reachable by keyboard, pointer, touch and assistive tech. Use it when building a bordered input, not for field-level messaging.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useInputStatusIcon

name:        useLightbox
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Lightbox
description: State management and accessible trigger wiring for Lightbox. Eliminates boilerplate for managing open state and current index. Returns trigger props with button role, tabIndex={0}, aria-haspopup="dialog", and keyboard activation handlers, along with a pre-wired Lightbox element that handles dismissal, next/previous navigation, and focus restoration.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useLightbox

name:        usePanGesture
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Reports a drag on an element as values, for a surface the product moves itself: a card that follows the finger, a drawer pulled by its handle. A finger, a mouse and a pen all drive it. A mouse or pen drag that starts on selectable text selects that text, and the pan reports nothing. Give that text `user-select: none`. The drag claims its touch at UIKit's 10 pt, as `UIPanGestureRecognizer` does, so a tap stays a tap, and a press or a long press is never reported as a pan. With `axis`, a scroll across that axis that starts on the element stays the page's; without it, the pan takes a drag in any direction, so a finger's scroll that starts on the element moves the element instead of the page. A trackpad scroll still scrolls the page. The hook is a thin layer over `createPanGesture`, the same API for code without React. A drag has no keyboard or assistive-technology path of its own: whatever the drag does needs another way to do it, such as buttons or arrow keys (WCAG 2.5.7). The pan moves nothing itself, so Reduce Motion applies to the motion you drive from it: honor the user's reduced-motion setting in the animation that moves the element. Where a component already offers the behavior, use its prop instead: BottomSheet's `snapPoints`, Carousel's `hasSnap`.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook usePanGesture

name:        usePopover
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/Popover
description: Headless hook for click-triggered popovers with focus trapping. Combines useLayer with useFocusTrap, auto-focus, light dismiss, Escape handling, and an optional hidden close button for accessible dialog-like popover behavior. Every painted surface emits the canonical popover target. A custom composition needing a distinct stable seam should pass and document its own surfaceTarget.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook usePopover

name:        useTableGroupedRows
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableGroupedRows

name:        useTableTreeData
domain:      hook
package:     @astryxdesign/core
import:      @astryxdesign/core/hooks
description: Headless tree plugin for Table: renders nested rows with per-level indentation and expand/collapse chevrons in the tree column (the first column by default), and reflects hierarchy with aria-level on body rows and aria-expanded on each expand/collapse button. Composable with the other Table plugins: the canonical plugin order places tree before selection, so the checkbox column lands left of the indented tree column. Feed it the treeConfig from useTableTreeState, or construct the config directly for server-driven or pre-flattened trees. When no row is expandable (flat data), every transform is a pass-through and the table renders identically to one without the plugin. Known limitation: the tree column wraps its cell content, so textOverflow="truncate" tooltips do not apply within the tree column.
command:     npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 hook useTableTreeData
